newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CHANCE FOR FEYENOORD TO DENT PSV HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CHANCE FOR FEYENOORD TO DENT PSV HOPES.

text.p: Feyenoord Rotterdam's match against PSV Eindhoven on Sunday is one they need to win, both to restore pride and to prevent PSV from running away with the Dutch championship.
PSV stunned the Rotterdammers in Eindhoven in October, sticking seven goals past a 10-man Feyenoord, running riot with five goals in the second half.
That match had added significance in that it saw PSV move past Feyenoord and go into top spot in the league, a position they have maintained ever since.

A PSV win on Sunday would give them a six-point lead, while a victory for second-placed Feyenoord would put the two level at the top and ensure a tense battle between them in the final 10 matches of the season. Both teams are already out of Europe, but the title seems almost certain to go to one of them, with last season's champions Ajax Amsterdam foundering in fifth place.
Only one other team, Twente Enschede, remain in the title hunt but few believe they have the stamina or the squad for the season's tough last two months.
At Feyenoord's Stadium de Kuip, history favours the home side. Of the last 10 league matches between the two, Rotterdam have won four. The other six have all been drawn.
Feyenoord will have the benefit of raucous local support and they will not lack commitment and passion.

The flip-side of the coin is that their self-control can go in tense encounters. Feyenoord have gone down both at Ajax and PSV, but more worryingly have lost their nerve in both fixtures. Red cards reduced them to 10 men on each occasion.
PSV, by contrast, have shown greater poise in the big games, having already beaten Feyenoord and Ajax. They also show more attacking flair and have a far superior goal difference.
The combination of the imaginative midfielder Wim Jonk and the accurate punch of Luc Nilis's shots has given PSV 66 goals, 26 more than Feyenoord.
PSV's fullbacks add to their attacking options with frequent charges up the wing. However, their defence can seem porous, particularly as experienced centre back Stan Valckx now lacks pace.

Feyenoord's defence have suffered some monumental lapses, notably at PSV in November and more recently at Ajax, but their strength comes from the back. The experience and precise passing of the 33-year-old Ronald Koeman could prise open PSV's defence, particularly as gaps open up on the flank for Gaston Taument to weave his way forward.
However, quite who the defences must contend with still remains in doubt as both teams have worrying injuries to their key attackers.
PSV's Nilis has been out for a week and a half with an ankle injury although he resumed light training on Tuesday.

The Belgian striker was last year's leading scorer and heads the field this year with 15 goals. Last season, he was named player of the year in the Netherlands and Belgium. He is vital to PSV's challenge and seems bound to play, but any hint that he is below par will comfort Feyenoord and his man-marker, mostly likely to be George Boateng.
The Rotterdammers are struggling to restore Henryk Larsson to full fitness after a back injury. The young Swedish striker is Feyenoord's top scorer, albeit with only five league goals.
He went on for a spell during last weekend's 2-0 defeat of bottom club NEC Nijmegen and Feyenoord will hope the dreadlocked figure will be able to team up with Taument and cut through PSV's defence.
Feyenoord, however, will definitely have the services of fiery Pablo Sanchez. The Argentine striker was sent off for a head-butt in the 3-0 loss at Ajax and was due for suspension.
Feyenoord appealed and learnt on Tuesday that the appeal cannot be heard before Sunday's game. So Sanchez plays.
